name: Calgary
industries: Energy megaprojects and the transition portfolio dominate, with a growing downtown tech sector diversifying demand.
intro:
Calgary's project culture was forged in the oil sands: megaproject delivery, joint-venture governance and formal stage gates are native skills here, and PMP is the credential that certifies them. The energy transition is now redirecting that muscle — carbon capture, hydrogen and renewables programs draw on the same certified talent — while a deliberate economic diversification push has built a genuine tech scene downtown. Live online batches run year-round with sensible Calgary timings — a full Saturday–Sunday weekend cohort plus a midweek Wednesday–Thursday option — so you train during comfortable local daytime hours; the schedule table below lists every upcoming date with its exact Calgary start and finish. The package stays identical: live weekend instruction, methodical exam application support, full-length mocks, and open trainer access until you pass.

Calgary's project economy is re-tooling in real time: traditional energy majors still run some of North America's largest capital programs, while the energy-transition and tech diversification push adds new delivery structures alongside. Both eras of the market speak stage-gate governance, and certified project leadership moves between them freely. The course runs live online over two consecutive days shown in Calgary local time on this page — no Deerfoot drive to a venue. Energy-sector project compensation in Calgary has its own scale and cycles; the sourced entries in the salary table below keep your numbers current and named. The employer list reflects the energy-and-diversification mix, and operators staffing new capital programs can certify project teams through private cohorts.
